items: T5 Judgment — Confirm affected-path merged and closed/rejected prior art for flow.py and integrate.py — the supplied snapshot exposes one synthetic commit, no remotes, and none of the cited #739 iteration records, so the required historical comparison cannot be established (review-prior-art.log:1; brief.md:17).

**The patch adds a fourth outcome the brief's (i)-(iii) do not define.** That outcome is the `past` hold: update the held branch from the base (`integrate.py:1971`, `:1977-1982`; `flow.py:1626-1632`).

`template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:1949-1952`, `:1977-1982`: the patch adds a third outcome the brief does not list, the `past` hold. A line bundle doesn't merge onto the base the head holds but does merge onto `<remote>/main` now, and the head is told to "update <name>'s branch from <remote>/main" (`flow.py:1626`). The brief's rule (iii) says "anything else stops as today". Probe (3b) does want that advice text, and the brief allowed (3b) to take another path, so this is a defensible reading. Still, it turns a class of former `STOPPING` runs into holds that the brief never specified. The test file shows this: `test_main_undid_the_commit_…` was red before the fix because it stopped. Confirm that this extra hold kind is wanted in this child, and is not a separate change.

`template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:1962-1966` with `template/tests/test_flow_cross_wave_stranded_holds.py:498`: in case (3c), A's branch on the line no longer merges onto the current `origin/main`, but Y gets only the ordinary overlap advice. The test asserts that "rebuild issue_A's branch" is **absent**. The brief says Y gets the overlap advice "not only A's rebuild", which can be read as wanting both. As built, nothing in the run tells A's owner that A's branch no longer fits main. Decide whether that silence is the intended reading.

T5 Judgment — Confirm the approach against affected-file merged history and closed/rejected work — path searches found only the synthetic base, no remote, and no supplied rejected #739 artifacts, so duplication or a previous rejection cannot be settled here (review-prior-art.log:1; review-prior-art.log:11; brief.md:17).

**When the move and the held bundle's own change hit the same partner in the same file, the run still stops. Brief rule (ii) says it should be held.** The cause is the file-level test at `template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:2000` (`not set(files) - set(after)`), described at `:1953-1955`. Concrete case, run with real git in my sandbox on the case (1) fixture: base `shared.txt` = nine lines; A (wave 0) edits lines 2 and 8; after fold 1, main edits line 8; W (`Depends on: Z`, built on the moved main) edits line 2. Result: `wave 1 did not integrate (issue_W's branch … conflicts in shared.txt) … STOPPING`, holds `{}`, and T is never built. The two-file version of the same situation (A adds `a.txt` and edits `shared.txt` line 2; main adds `a.txt`; W edits line 2) is held with both steps: "rebuild issue_A's branch on the new origin/main" plus the `Conflicts with: A` proposal. To a user these are the same situation, but one stops and one holds. The stop is the old behaviour, so the advice is never wrong. It is still a gap against rule (ii): A does not merge onto `S`, and W's own change does. No test pins this stop, and the test file's list of cases that "still stop" (`test_flow_cross_wave_stranded_holds.py:26-30`) does not mention it. Decision needed: accept the stop as rule (iii), or ask for a hunk-level test (compare the conflict hunks, not the file names) so this case holds too.

T5 Judgment — Confirm affected-file merged history and closed/rejected work do not supersede or contradict this fix — the artifact-only target has one synthetic base commit, no remote, and none of the cited rejected patches, so that prior-art decision remains unsettled (review-prior-art.log:1; brief.md:17).

**The same clash holds or stops depending on whether it spans one file or two.** `integrate.py:1996-2002` counts the move as part of the clash only when the conflict with the rebuilt partner "loses a file" (the docstring at `integrate.py:1953-1955` says so). Concrete case (real-git probe on the case-(1) shape): base `shared.txt` = `NINE`. A edits lines 2 and 8. After fold 1, main edits line 8. W (`Depends on: Z`, built on that main) keeps main's line 8 and edits line 2. Result: `wave 1 did not integrate (issue_W's branch … (conflicts in shared.txt)) … STOPPING`, holds `{}`. Now split the same situation over two files: A changes `a.txt` + `shared.txt` line 2, main adds `a.txt`, W keeps main's `a.txt` and edits line 2. That version is held with the right two-step advice: "rebuild issue_A's branch on the new origin/main … declare `Conflicts with: A` … rebuild issue_W on a base that holds issue_A". This is the shape of the flipped test at `template/tests/test_flow_cross_wave_fold_holds.py:404`. The brief's rule (ii) ("partner's head does not merge onto S alone while the head's own change does") covers both. Only the file count separates them. The one-file case is a safe stop (the pre-#749 behaviour, no wrong advice), and no success-criterion case needs it. The human should decide whether to accept it as a known limit, or ask for a hunk-level comparison (a design change, not a quick fix). It is not worth an auto-iterate round on its own.
